'''Tanya Khovanova''' ({{lang|ru|Татьяна Гелиевна Хованова}}, also spelled Tatyana Hovanova; born 25 January 1959) is an American [[mathematician]] of Russian origin who became the second female gold medalist at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]s. She is a lecturer in mathematics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].

== Education ==
As a high school student, Khovanova became a member of the Soviet team for the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] (IMO). In the summer of 1975, [[Valery Senderov]] gave the team a list of difficult [[mathematical problem]]s used in the entrance exams of Moscow State University to discriminate against [[Soviet Jew]]s, a topic she later wrote about.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://io9.gizmodo.com/how-to-solve-jewish-math-problems-5848752|title=How to solve "Jewish" math problems|last=Gonzalez|first=Robbie|date=October 11, 2011|work= [[Gizmodo]] |access-date=2019-09-08}}</ref> Khovanova won the silver medal at the 1975 IMO, and a gold medal at the 1976 Olympiad. Her finish at the 1976 Olympiad was second among all competitors,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=12663|title=Tanya Khovanova|work=International Mathematical Olympiad results|access-date=2019-09-07}}</ref> the highest achievement for female students until 1984, when Karin Gröger from [[East Germany]] tied for the first place.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=9572|title=Karin Gröger|work=International Mathematical Olympiad results|access-date=2019-09-07}}</ref>

Khovanova graduated with honors from [[Moscow State University]] (MSU) with a master's degree in mathematics in 1981. She completed her [[Ph.D.]] at MSU in 1988 with [[Israel Gelfand]] as her doctoral advisor.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=84448}}</ref>

== Career ==
Khovanova left the Soviet Union in 1990, and worked for several years in Israel and the US as a postdoctoral researcher. However, she stopped working as a researcher to raise her children, and then worked in the [[telecommunications]] and [[military contracting]] industry, before returning to academia as a lecturer at [[MIT]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B2rXxbFqvn3ZLWdrb1JsaDNvNndDdXA4NndQVXVlbEkxZ2lJ/view|title=To count the natural numbers|first=Emily|last=Jia|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|year=2016}}</ref>

Khovanova has been a mathematics competition coach at the [[Advanced Math and Science Academy Charter School]] in [[Marlborough, Massachusetts]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=131|title=Tanya Khovanova|publisher=MIT Mathematics Department|access-date=2019-09-07|archive-date=2019-09-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190918220127/http://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=131|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2010, she helped found the MIT PRIMES program for after school mentoring of local high school students, and she continues to serve as its head mentor. She is also head mentor for mathematics of the [[Research Science Institute]], a summer research program for high school students at MIT.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Etingof|first1=Pavel|author1-link=Pavel Etingof|last2=Gerovitch|first2=Slava|author2-link=Slava Gerovitch|last3=Khovanova|first3=Tanya|date=September 2015|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|pages=910–918|title=Mathematical Research in High School: The PRIMES Experience|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201508/rnoti-p910.pdf|volume=62|issue=8|doi=10.1090/noti1270|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Research ===
In Khovanova's earlier mathematical research, she studied [[representation theory]], the theory of [[integrable system]]s, [[quantum group]] theory, and [[superstring theory]]. Her later work explores [[combinatorics]] and [[recreational mathematics]].<ref name=":0" />

===Online activities===
In the mid-1990s Khovanova created a website called Number Gossip, about the special properties of individual numbers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/2010/03/09/website_explains_the_mystery_of_numbers.html|title=Website explains the mystery of numbers|newspaper=[[Toronto Star]]|first=Debra|last=Black|date=March 9, 2010}}</ref> In 2007, she created a mathematics blog, centered on mathematical puzzles and problem solving.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/a-blog-around-the-clock/the-scienceblogging-weekly-june-8th-2012/|title=The Scienceblogging Weekly (June 8th, 2012)|date=June 8, 2012|first=Bora|last=Zivkovic|publisher= [[Scientific American]] }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
When Khovanova emigrated to [[Boston]], she did not know how to drive. A friend gave her a copy of ''[[The Boston Driver's Handbook]]'' which she studied to learn tips before learning years later that the book was intended to be humorous.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/35733400/the_boston_globe/|title=50 words|last=Khovanova|first=Tanya|date=2018-12-16|website= [[Boston Globe]] |language=en|via=Newspapers.com|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-08}}</ref> She has two sons; her first was born in the [[Soviet Union]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://blog.tanyakhovanova.com/2017/02/russian-and-american-children/|title=Russian and American Children|last=Khovanova|first=Tanya|date=2017-02-10|website=Tanya Khovanova's Math Blog|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-09-08}}</ref>

==Recognition==
An essay about Khovanova, "To Count the Natural Numbers," by Emily Jia, won the 2016 Essay Contest of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160912031020/sites.google.com/site/awmmath/programs/essay-contest/2016-results|archive-date=2016-09-12|url=https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/programs/essay-contest/2016-results|title=Results of 2016 Essay Contest|work=AWM Programs: Essay Contest|publisher= [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] |access-date=2019-09-07}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Jia |first1=Emily |title=2016 Student Essay Contest High School Winner |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/student-essay-contest/2016-student-essay-contest-results/2016-student-essay-contest-high-school-winner/ |website= [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM) |access-date=6 May 2023}}</ref>

==Selected works==
Two of Khovanova's papers were included in the annual ''Best Writing on Mathematics'' volumes, in 2014 and 2016 respectively.<ref>{{Cite book|title=The best writing on mathematics, 2014| last = Pitici | first = Mircea |date=23 November 2014|isbn=9781400865307|location=Princeton|oclc=894169899}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=The best writing on mathematics. 2016|others=Pitici, Mircea, 1965-|date=7 March 2017|isbn=9780691175294|location=Princeton, New Jersey|oclc=958799818}}</ref>
